reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended A critical merge bug routes anonymous argument fragments from parallel unindexed calls into the last call, leaving the first empty and corrupting the second call’s JSON.
1 open issue - [Anonymous argument fragments merge into the last parallel call](https://github.com/posit-dev/chatlas/pull/474#discussion_r4519563105) · New
What changed in this PR This PR updates the shared streaming merge utility to join index-free tool-call fragments from OpenAI-compatible servers. **Changes:** - Merge anonymous tool-call fragments into the preceding unindexed call. - Guard index comparisons against missing keys and non-dictionary entries. - Add four regression tests and document the behavior in the changelog. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `tests/​test_utils_merge.py` | Adds coverage for fragment joining, distinct IDs, mixed indexing, and empty lists. | | `chatlas/​_merge.py` | Adds fragment detection and fallback merging; guards index comparisons. | | `CHANGELOG.md` | Documents the streaming tool-call fixes. |
Review effort: Balanced

### 🔵 Needs a closer look Tool-call fragment routing mishandles missing indices, absent arguments, and parallel calls, causing requests to split or argument JSON to become corrupted. **No open issues** 🎉
3 previously missed issues In code that hasn't changed since last review
Reject ambiguous anonymous fragments for parallel calls `chatlas/​_merge.py:114` JSON completeness cannot identify which parallel call an anonymous fragment belongs to. After two calls are announced with empty arguments, interleaved fragments `'{"x":'`, `'{"y":'`, `'1}'`, and `'2}'` all merge into the first call, corrupting its JSON and leaving the second empty. Use an explicit routing signal, or restrict this fallback to a single in-flight call and report ambiguity otherwise.
Merge unindexed fragments into indexed calls `chatlas/​_merge.py:136` If the initial tool-call chunk includes `index=0` but subsequent argument fragments omit `index`, this predicate excludes the existing call from every merge target. An initial argument string `'{"x":'` followed by `'1}'` therefore becomes two calls instead of one valid request. Allow indexed calls as merge targets while keeping the missing-index restriction on incoming fragments, and add a regression case for this mixed stream.
Treat missing arguments as incomplete tool-call payloads `chatlas/​_merge.py:142` Missing or null arguments mean a call is still awaiting its arguments, not that its JSON is complete. If two unindexed calls are announced with only ids and names, subsequent argument objects both fall back to the last call, leaving the first empty and producing invalid JSON such as `{"x":1}{"y":2}` in the second. Treat absent/null arguments as incomplete and add a regression case for these headers.
1 resolved since last review - [Anonymous argument fragments merge into the last parallel call](https://github.com/posit-dev/chatlas/pull/474#discussion_r4519563105)
Review effort: Balanced

### 🔵 Needs a closer look Anonymous argument fragments can be silently routed to the wrong tool call, and reparsing accumulated arguments adds quadratic decoding work to single-call streaming. **No open issues** 🎉
2 previously missed issues In code that hasn't changed since last review
Reject ambiguous anonymous arguments instead of guessing the target `chatlas/​_merge.py:116` The first-unfinished-call heuristic can silently route arguments to the wrong function when parallel calls send their arguments in reverse announcement order. It also breaks sequential calls: after `f(arguments="")` and `g(arguments='{"x":')`, an anonymous `1}` is assigned to `f`, although `load_tool_request_args()` accepts empty arguments as `{}`. Use explicit routing metadata or a verified ordering contract, and reject ambiguous streams rather than inferring the target solely from JSON completeness.
Avoid reparsing accumulated arguments for single-target streams `chatlas/​_merge.py:119` Every anonymous fragment reparses the accumulated arguments even when there is only one possible tool-call target, adding quadratic JSON-decoding work to single-call streaming. With 64-byte fragments, doubling the argument payload from 64 KiB to 128 KiB increased the text decoded from roughly 32 MiB to 128 MiB. Bypass the completeness check for a single target, reserving it for cases where routing actually requires it.
Review effort: Balanced

### 🟡 Changes recommended Unindexed calls announced with empty argument strings are incorrectly marked complete, causing subsequent fragments to accumulate in the last call and produce invalid JSON.
1 open issue - [Empty argument announcements misroute parallel tool-call fragments](https://github.com/posit-dev/chatlas/pull/474#discussion_r4519719133) · New
Review effort: Balanced

### 🟢 Approval recommended No active review issues block the streamed tool-call assembly improvements.
1 open issue - [Empty argument announcements misroute parallel tool-call fragments](https://github.com/posit-dev/chatlas/pull/474#discussion_r4519719133)
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: When two unindexed calls are announced together and a later delta contains an anonymous argument fragment for each, both fragments are merged into the last call. For example, fragments `{"x":1}` and `{"y":2}` leave the first call empty and give the second invalid JSON, so keeping distinct initial IDs does not preserve parallel continuations. Define an explicit association strategy or reject ambiguous continuations, and add a regression test with two incomplete calls followed by their fragments.

If two unindexed calls are announced with `arguments=""` before their ordered argument fragments, both are marked complete and every fragment is routed to the last call. For payloads `{"x":1}` and `{"y":2}`, this produces `['', '{"x":1}{"y":2}']`, leaving invalid JSON. Treat empty strings as possible pending placeholders while prioritizing an already-started incomplete payload, and add a parallel-routing regression case for empty-string announcements.

This is the other horn of an unavoidable ambiguity. An announced `arguments: ""` is wire-identical for two situations: a complete empty payload (chatlas parses it as `{}` downstream) and a call still awaiting argument fragments. Treating `""` as incomplete — the previous revision — routed a following call's fragments into the empty-args call, corrupting the common sequential pattern `f(arguments="")` → `g(arguments='{"x":')` → fragment `1}` (covered by `test_fragment_after_an_empty_arguments_call_routes_to_the_active_call`). Treating it as complete misroutes the parallel-announced-with-empty-strings ordering you describe instead. No routing rule satisfies both, and a server that omits `index` can only stream coherently in announcement order — `index` is precisely the field that demarcates parallel calls — so the code optimizes for the sequential ordering and documents the limitation in `_merge.py`.
